question: The angle between the incident ray and the emergent ray of a prism is called:
solution: The correct answer is __**Angle of deviation**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Angle of deviation** is defined as the angle between the incident ray and the emergent ray after passing through the prism. It measures the bending of light due to the prism. • When light enters the prism, it undergoes **refraction**, bending towards the normal at the first surface, and again bending away from the normal at the second surface. This results in the deviation of light from its original path. • The **angle of deviation** depends on the **angle of incidence**, the material of the prism (refractive index), and the angle of the prism. A larger refractive index or angle of the prism results in a larger deviation. • The minimum angle of deviation (δₘᵢₙ) occurs when the light ray passes symmetrically through the prism, i.e., when the angle of incidence equals the angle of emergence. • The formula for the angle of deviation is: δ = i + e - A Where: i = Angle of incidence e = Angle of emergence A = Angle of the prism
